children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--The ICE Futures canola market traded higher for most of the session before buying interest subsided and values drifted lower in sympathy with the sharp declines in Chicago soyoil on Tuesday.
January canola was down C$2.60 at C$773.20 per tonne after trading as high as C$783.10 per tonne.
European rapeseed was also weaker, although gains in Chicago soybeans and Malaysian palm oil provided some support.

Canadian processors crushed 1.13 million tonnes of canola in October, reported Statistics Canada. That took the marketing year-to-date total through three months to 3.6 million tonnes - up from 2.9 million tonnes in 2025-26.

U.S. markets will be closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and only open for reduced hours on Friday, while canola will continue to trade its usual hours. Positioning ahead of the U.S. holiday was a feature of the trade.
There were 50,695 contracts traded on Tuesday, which compares with Monday when 50,426 contracts changed hands.
Spreading accounted for 26,988 of the contracts traded.
